newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs mostly off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs mostly off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were mostly $0.50 per cwt lower on Thursday as weak demand continued to weigh on values, livestock dealers said.

They noted widespread talk there would be a very light Saturday kill this week while several plants may be taking a floating holiday on Monday. Hog runs were more than sufficient to meet current sluggish demand.
Early trade in the key Iowa/south Minnesota area was reported at $55.00 and $55.50 per cwt in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 to plants, down $0.50 from prices paid for similar hogs on Wednesday.
USDA reported a top in Iowa-southern Minnesota on Wednesday of $57.50 per cwt, a drop of $4.00 since July 22.
Dealers noted hog weights were falling slightly, although they remained above year-ago levels.
USDA reported an average hog weight in Iowa-south Minnesota for the week to July 26 of 250 lbs, down from 250.9 lbs a week earlier but above 244.8 lbs in the same week a year ago.
